newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union to hold day of protest at sick cuts.
newsitem.headline: German union to hold day of protest at sick cuts.

text.p: Germany's largest trade union said tens of thousands of workers across Bavaria would stage a day of protest on Monday after firms vowed to implement new legislation cutting sick pay to 80 percent of salaries.

IG Metall engineering and metalworkers union called on its members to join a rally outside the gates of the Audi car factory in the northern Bavarian city of Ingolstadt and to brace themselves for more industrial action later this year.
Monday's day of protest comes as the latest in a series which have included unspecified stoppages and disrupted production at German companies, but which have stopped short of all-out strike action.

The protests target a new law that came into force in October as part of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's austerity drive aimed at helping Germany fulfil strict fiscal requirements to qualify for a single European currency due for launch in 1999.
Protests have gone ahead despite earlier promises by employers not to introduce the 20 percent sick pay cut until wider agreement with unions had been reached.

Werner Neugebauer, head of IG Metall in Bavaria, said his union had cancelled existing wage agreements with effect from January 31 and warned firms that workers could go on strike from the end of February over the issue, if necessary.
But Neugebauer said he was in favour of talks with employers before considering strike action.
The Bavarian branch of IG Metall, which represents some 650,000 of the total 3.5 million workers employed in the sector, cancelled existing wage contracts in October.
